items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I joined the Lionel Hampton band, they had some more experienced musicians in there, because Lionel Hampton had more money to work with.

ctx.x: Let’s go back to the history stuff. I think there will be a parallel current, because you are such a philosopher, or have such a philosophy about life and about how music should be, how it should go, and what’s involved with it. I saw that in what you were giving to the students today. You were giving them life lessons, and much of what you are sharing with us, are life lessons, beyond the facts of the matter – the essence of the matter, which is the life lessons. That seems to be very paramount to you, very…

Buddy was giving me an opportunity to write and play. I was always looking for something that could help me further my knowledge about music and about playing. When I joined the Lionel Hampton band, they had some more experienced musicians in there, because Lionel Hampton had more money to work with.
So Lionel Hampton was the next big . . . ?

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: after I wrote for Buddy Johnson I wrote for Lionel Hampton and I wrote for Maynard

ctx.x: I mean do you need to be near a piano?

I used to write without the piano. I wrote a lot of the arrangements, after I wrote for Buddy Johnson I wrote for Lionel Hampton and I wrote for Maynard. And a lot of the arrangements I wrote for Maynard I wrote without the piano. And those are recorded things. I was a young guy, you know, I had the energy that it takes to actually do that.
Well speaking of that, I have to play something for you. Because it’s something I really think is —
